outcome: presence and characteristics of microbial signals/bacteria
positive aerobic and anaerobic clinical cultures
cohort: The study included healthy term infants from whom fetal meconium (collected during elective breech C-sections), first-pass neonatal meconium, and infant stool samples were obtained, alongside technical and procedural controls.
finding: No microbial signal distinct from negative controls was detected in fetal meconium, leading to the conclusion that fetal gut colonization does not occur before birth in healthy term infants and neonatal meconium profiles reflect populations acquired during and after birth.
cross-section timing: Samples were collected before birth (during elective C-section), hours to days after birth (first-pass meconium), and later in infancy (infant stool).
